title: CRLA/330/2015 of Hari Singh Alias Bablu AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No. 330 of 2015
1. Hari Singh @ Bablu S/o Amar Singh
2. Kamal Singh S/o Ratan Singh ....... Appellants
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand .......Respondent
Present : Ms. Pushpa Joshi, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Chetna Latwal,
Advocate for appellant Hari Singh @ Bablu.
Mr. S.R.S. Gill, Advocate for appellant Kamal Singh.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, Deputy Advocate General assisted by Ms. Mamta
Joshi, Brief Holder and Mr. Pankaj Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.

Coram: Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
 Hon'ble Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.
Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 This criminal appeal has been preferred by the
appellants against the judgment and order dated
16.09.2015 passed by the learned Sessions Judge,
Nainital in Session Trial No. 141 of 2014, whereby the
appellants have been convicted under Section 302 of
I.P.C. read with Section 34 IPC and have been sentenced
to imprisonment for life and fine of Rs. 25,000/- each,
and in default of payment of fine to undergo further
imprisonment for a period of two years.
2. Brief facts of the case as per the prosecution
are that the deceased Pooja and the appellant Hari Singh
@ Bablu (who will be referred hereinafter only as Bablu for
the sake of convenience), were in their early twenties at
the relevant time and were known to each other. Pooja
had about eight months prior to the present incident
(when Pooja was allegedly killed at the hands of Bablu),
lodged an FIR against Bablu. Later efforts were made by
village elders and a "Panchayat" took place where a
compromise was reached between the parties. As per the
compromise between the parties, the accused Bablu
promised to marry Pooja. Based on the compromised

2
arrived at between the parties a final report was filed by
the police. The final report though was yet to be accepted
by the learned Magistrate, and the date fixed by the court
was 29.09.2014.
3. Meanwhile, on 23.08.2014, in the evening,
Pooja (deceased) received a phone call from the accused,
who asked her to come near the Poplar fields, which was
about 400 mts. from her house. The deceased went to the
appointed place with her 15 year old younger sister
named Ms. Ganga. About 20-30 yards ahead of the Poplar
fields near a culvert, she asked her sister to stay put and
she alone proceeded towards the poplar fields, where she
had an appointment with her assailants, as Bablu was
waiting for her, in the field, along with his friend Kamal.
Kamal holds the hands of the deceased and Bablu slits
open her throat. Pooja falls on the ground, in a pool of
blood, and the two accused run away from the spot. The
eyewitness to the incident, the younger sister of the
deceased Ms. Ganga first rushed to the place, where her
sister was lying dead and then she runs to her house and
informs her father and uncle, who were present in the
house.
4. An FIR was lodged immediately thereafter. In
the FIR, however, only the accused Hari Singh @ Bablu is
named, along with three "unknown persons". There is a
narration of the events, already been stated above. There
is no mention of Kamal. The inquest started at 11:45 p.m.
on 23.08.2014 and continued till early hours in the next
morning. As per the opinion of the "Panchas" the throat of
deceased was slit open which resulted in her death.
5. Subsequently, however, in the investigation
which commenced the next day i.e. 24.08.2014, the

3
statements of the complainant PW 1 (father of the
deceased) and Ms. Ganga PW 5 (younger sister of the
deceased) were recorded. PW 5 in her statement says that
she and her sister went to the poplar fields where her
sister confronted two persons. One was Hari Singh @
Bablu and another was Kamal Singh. She knows Kamal
who is the co-accused as he had come to her village along
with main accused Bablu, even prior to the incident. She
did not tell the name of Kamal to her father, immediately
after the incident last night, as she was traumatized.
6. A similar statement has been given by the PW 1
who is the complainant and the father of the deceased.
7. The accused Bablu was arrested on 24.08.2014
and the accused Kamal Singh was arrested on
25.08.2014. At the behest of main accused Bablu,
recovery of T-shirt, Jeans and "Angocha" was made from
the box of his double bed. All the three garments were
stained with blood. The next recovery made from this
particular witness is the knife and the stone, which were
used in the commission of crime. Both the knife and stone
were recovered from the paddy field near the place of
occurrence. They were sent for forensic examination, the
report of which will be perused in a while.
8. After investigation, the police filed its
chargesheet on 16.11.2014, and the matter was
committed to sessions as Session Trial No. 141 of 2014
"State v. Hari Singh @ Bablu & another". Subsequently,
the trial court framed charges against the accused under
Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC.
9. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has
examined as many as nine witnesses. Out of these
witnesses, PW 1 Pooran Singh (the complainant and the

4
father of the deceased), PW 2 Veer Singh who is another
witness of last seen and brother of the complainant, PW 5
Ms. Ganga Devi (sister of the deceased) and PW 6 Dr.
Janendra Kumar Jha, who conducted autopsy on the
body of the deceased are principal witnesses.
10. PW 1 in his examination in chief states that the
deceased Pooja was his daughter and was 24 year of age
at the time of the incident. The accused Bablu and his
daughter were in a relationship and Bablu had promised
to marry her, though he continued to sexually exploit her
daughter and later refused to marry her. Under these
circumstances, his daughter had lodged a first
information report regarding rape against the accused
Bablu at Police Station Bazpur on 21.01.2014.
Consequent to the FIR, mediation took place between the
two families through the members of their community*.
During mediations the accused Bablu tendered his
apologies and requested the prosecutrix to take back the
case against him, and in return he promised to marry her.
This resulted in a compromise between the parties and
thereafter a final report was filed by the police in the
court. Meanwhile, Bablu again refused to fulfill his
promise, and as a result, Pooja had warned accused
Bablu that she will give evidence against him in the court.
PW 1 further states that in the case of rape, the date fixed
was 18.08.2014 in the Ramnagar court. Bablu, however,
did not turn up on that day and the next date fixed was
29.09.2014. Since Bablu was sure that on his refusal to
marry Pooja, she should give evidence against him in
*Incidentally, it has come in the evidence that both the accused Hari
Singh @ Bablu and the deceased belong to "Buksa" community, which is a
tribal community in the Terai area of Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar
districts in Uttarakhand.

5
court (in the case of rape), he called Pooja in the
agricultural field on that fateful day, in order to kill her.
The time was about 07:00 p.m. on 23.08.2014 when Pooja
along with her younger sister Ganga had gone to the exact
place in the field with the poplar trees, having been invited
by the accused. PW 1 further states that after some time,
his daughter Ganga @ Soni came crying and said that
near the Poplar field of Sohan Dhillon, Bablu had come
along with his other friends and has slit open the throat of
her sister and had killed her. On this information, he
along with other persons of the village, whom he names as
Veer Singh, Cheda Singh, Arjun Singh & Ranjeet Singh,
went to the spot and found the dead body of his daughter.
He further states that the accused was seen running from
the spot by Veer Singh.* This witness further says that the
FIR was lodged on 23.08.2014 at 09:35 p.m. at P.S.
Ramnagar. The FIR was lodged by narrating the above
events to the police personnel. He recognized the copy of
the FIR, which was shown to him, as well as the signature
which was there on the FIR. This witness then continues
his examination-in-chief stating that the inquest had
begun on 23.08.2014 in the night itself and that he was
one of the witnesses to the inquest report. He then states
that after the incident, his younger daughter Ganga who
had witnessed the murder, was totally traumatized and
scared, and was continuously sobbing. The next day when
he inquired from her as to who were the "other persons",
along with Bablu, she said that along with Bablu there
was only one other person, and he was Kamal Singh S/o
* Veer Singh is incidentally the younger brother of
PW 1/complainant.

6
Ratan Singh, who is friend of Bablu and resides in the
same village as Bablu. Ganga also informed him that
Kamal had caught hold of the deceased Pooja while Bablu
had slit her throat. This witness recognized Kamal in the
court and said that he used to come to his house, prior to
the incident as well.
11. The examination-in-chief of PW 1 was done on
01.05.2015. It appears that on that day, the defence was
asked to cross-examine the witness, which they denied
and the opportunity was closed. The records, however,
show that this witness was called again by the court and
was cross-examined by the defence on 22.07.2015.
Questions were asked about the mobile phone (police has
not recovered either the mobile phone of the accused
Bablu or the deceased), to which this witness says that
mobile phone was taken by his daughter when she went
to the poplar fields on that fateful day and he suspects
that the accused persons took away her mobile phone
with them, while escaping from the spot. He admits that
he too has a mobile phone with him, but he does not
know his phone no., as he is illiterate, and the mobile was
purchased by his daughter from the prize she has received
from the school. He denies that he had actually heard the
conversation of his daughter while she was talking with
Bablu on phone, as whenever she used to talk on phone
she used to take the mobile phone inside the house. In his
cross-examination, he admits the compromise which
arrived at between the parties, after the FIR of rape. He
admits that he received the information about the death of
his elder daughter from his younger daughter Ganga, who
had accompanied the deceased to the agricultural field on
that fateful day. Questions were also put to this witness
by the defence that he was against the marriage and

7
therefore a suggestion was also made that it was he who
killed his daughter. A case of honour killing was being
suggested by the defence. All the same, this is far from the
truth, inasmuch as it is an admitted fact that both the
accused as well as the deceased belong to same tribal
community called "Buksa", who are the original
inhabitants of Terai Bhabar area of Nainital and Udham
Singh Nagar, in Uttarakhand.
12. PW 2 Veer Singh is the uncle of the deceased.
He states in his examination-in-chief that on 23.08.2014,
in the evening, when he was throwing out the excess
water from his agricultural field, he saw Bablu and Kamal
Singh hurriedly making their way towards the farm of one
"Preetpal". These two persons used to visit their house, so
he did not find anything unusual in their presence. All the
same, when he reached his house, he was informed that
his niece has been murdered and his another niece Ganga
has informed that his sister has been killed by none other
than Bablu. This witness incidentally is also a witness of
the inquest report.
13. PW 5 Ganga, who is younger sister of the
deceased, is the star witness. In her examination-in-chief,
she says that at the time of the incident she was a student
of class X in Government Inter College Thari, Ramnagar.
She knows the accused persons Hari Singh @ Bablu and
Kamal and both of them are friends. She also recognized
them in the court. She then states that deceased was her
elder sister. On 21.01.2014, her sister had lodged a first
information report against Bablu for rape. On 18.08.2014,
the date was fixed in Ramnagar court. The deceased had
warned Bablu that if he refuses to marry her, she will give
evidence against him in the court (the final report had yet
to be accepted). On 23.08.2014, the accused Bablu had

8
called her sister on phone and said that he wants to talk
to her about their court marriage, and therefore she
should meet him near 'poplar fields', of Sohan Singh at
07:00 p.m. Her sister asked her to accompany her to the
field, i.e. the appointed place where she had to meet the
accused. As they came close to the poplar fields, she was
asked by her sister to stand put near the culvert. Her
sister went ahead towards the poplar field. At the same
time, Bablu and Kamal came out from the adjacent paddy
fields where they were waiting for her sister. Kamal caught
hold of her hands and Bablu took out a knife, with which
he slit open the throat of Pooja. She (i.e. PW 5) tried to
raise an alarm, on which Kamal asked her to keep quiet
otherwise she too will meet the same fate. Her sister fell
on the ground, and then Bablu lifted a stone lying nearby
with which he hit Pooja on her head and said that now
she should go and get married in heaven! Not only this, he
then spat on the face of the deceased. The two then ran
away towards the filed of Updesh Sharma. She first ran
towards her sister, who was lying dead, and then she
rushed towards her house and informed her parents
about the incident. Meanwhile, after hearing the noise
Ranjeet Singh, Veer Singh, Phool Singh and Arjun Singh
also came to our house and all of them went to the place
of occurrence. She further says that accused Kamal had
also come along with Bablu to her house prior to the
incident. After the incident, she was scared and
traumatized and for that reason she initially on the date of
the incident gave the name of Bablu only and not of
Kamal, but when she regained her balance the next day,
she gave the name of other co-accused i.e. Kamal to her
father and to the police, who took her statement the next
day.

9
14. Her examination in chief was done on
08.05.2015. This witness was cross-examined the same
day and then the case was adjourned and she was again
cross-examined after a period of about one month on
04.06.2015. She says that 'Bablu' had called her sister on
phone at about 05:00 p.m. She did not hear the exact
conversation between the two, all she knows is that Bablu
had called her sister, and asked her to meet him near the
Poplar field of the village. Later she along with her sister
went there, though she stood near the "pulia", and the
crime was committed about 10 steps ahead from where
she was standing. Her sister screamed and prayed with
the assailants not to kill her. On being questioned, this
witness denies that her sister had an affair with a person
called "Karan Singh". She also denies knowing any person
by this name. She admits that her sister had lodged a first
information report against the accused Bablu regarding
rape. She also denies that her sister was forcing Bablu to
marry her. Towards the end, this particular witness was
also examined by the court.
15. The post-mortem report shows four ante-mortem injuries on the body of the deceased, which are as
under:-
"(i) Incised wound over front of neck 3.5
cm. above manubrium sternum size 14 x 5 cm.
tapering both sides with cut of skin muscles,
both jugular veins, both external and internal
carotid arteries and partial cut of trachea (3/4
part) margin sharp, everted with clots.
(ii) Incised wound over scalp in right
parietal region size 6.5 x 3.5 cm. bone exposed
on cut section fracture of right parietal bone
with clots present.
(iii) Incised wound over scalp in 2 cm.
below and behind from the injury no. 2 size 4.5

10
x 2 cm. bone exposed, margin sharp on cut
section clot present.
(iv) incised wound over scalp in the mid
parietal region size 2.5 x 2.5 cm. bone exposed
margin sharp with tailing present."
16. The cause of death is shown as "ante-mortem
injuries leading to hemorrhage, shock & death".
17. PW 6 is Dr. Janendra Kumar Jha, who
conducted the postmortem on the body of the deceased.
This expert witness states before the court that out of four
ante-mortem injuries, ante-mortem injury nos. (i), (iii) &
(iv), can be caused by sharp edged weapon such as knife
or sword. Ante-mortem injury no. (ii) since also has
caused fracture of bone, may be caused by a heavy
weapon such as stone. This particular witness was also
shown the knife (exhibit A-10), which was used in the
commission of crime, and have blood stains on it. He
states that injury nos. (i), (iii) & (iv) could have been
caused by this knife. This witness was also shown another
bundle from which a curved stone, containing blood
stains on its edges, was taken out. This witness again
admitted that injury no. (ii) could have been caused by
this stone, as it is quite heavy and it could have also
caused the fracture which was on the skull of the
deceased.
18. Ms. Pushpa Joshi, learned Senior Counsel for
accused Bablu has argued that there is only one
eyewitness to the incident i.e. Ganga (PW 5). The first
information report has been filed on her narration as she
is the eyewitness, yet there is a different version in the
first information report and the statement of PW 5 which
was recorded the next day. Whereas in the first
information report, the names of Bablu and "three

11
unknown persons" have been mentioned, in the statement
given under Section 161 CrPC, this witness mentions the
names of Bablu and Kamal. This witness cannot be relied
upon and she is definitely is not an eyewitness, submits
the learned Senior Counsel. The learned Senior Counsel
has also raised her doubts in the manner in which the
recovery has been made, particularly in view of the fact
that there is no independent witness to the recovery. The
learned Senior Counsel would also argue that in any case
apart from the testimony of the eyewitness (PW 5), there is
no other evidence for the prosecution and based on the
evidence, conviction was not possible.
19. Mr. S.R.S. Gill, learned counsel for the co-accused Kamal Singh would argue that Kamal Singh has
not been named in the FIR. His name figures for the first
time in the statement under Section 161 CrPC given by
PW 1 and PW 5. The learned counsel would further argue
that the testimony of PW 2 who had seen the two accused
running from the spot, and who had named Kamal as the
accomplice of the main accused Bablu cannot be relied
upon for the reason that had he seen the two accused
running away from the spot, he would have definitely told
this fact to his elder brother, particularly in view of the
fact that this particular witness (who is the younger
brother of the complainant, and the uncle of the
deceased), had accompanied the complainant to the police
station to lodge the first information report and he is also
a witness to the inquest report.
20. The above facts, as stated by the learned
counsel for the appellant Kamal, are correct. PW 2 admits
that he had accompanied his elder brother PW 1 to the
police station for lodging the FIR. It is also an admitted
fact that PW 2 is a witness to the inquest report. There is,

12
however, no mention of the co-accused Kamal in the FIR!
PW 5 in her testimony has said that she knew Kamal very
well as he used to come to their house, along with Bablu.
Therefore had she actually seen him committing the
crime, she could not have missed him and she would have
said that to her father. Therefore, this appears to be an
afterthought by the prosecution and the presence of
Kamal seems to be doubtful. Moreover, no material
recovery has been shown from the appellant no. 2 (i.e.
Kamal Singh). The recovery of motorcycle which has been
shown, is of no consequence as it has not come in the
story of the prosecution that the motorcycle was ever used
in the commission of crime. It has not come in the
evidence of any of the witnesses that they have seen the
two accused either coming from the motorcycle or running
away in a motorcycle. The motorcycle which was recovered
belongs to his father, which was parked in his house,
therefore recovery of this motorcycle is not material at all.
21. Based on the evidence available on record, we
are of the view that though principally there is only one
eyewitness but her presence on the place of occurrence is
completely natural and we have no reason to doubt her
presence. What is also material in the present case is the
motive, which was there with the appellant Bablu, as a
first information report was lodged against him by the
deceased on allegation of rape and thereafter there was a
compromise, but since he was not willing to marry the
deceased he thought the easiest way to get out of it is to
kill her.
22. On 23.08.2014 he calls the deceased to a lonely
place in the agricultural field, more precisely near the
poplar fields. It was but natural for the deceased to have
confided this fact with her younger sister, and the two

13
going to the spot together. Asking her sister to stay put at
a distance, is also a natural conduct of an elder sister. We
have no reason to doubt the presence of PW 5 at the place
of occurrence. Her evidence to this extent, is trustworthy,
and inspires our confidence. Her testimony is further
corroborated by the recovery of clothes as well as the
weapons used in the crime, which have been recovered at
the behest of the accused Bablu. The clothes and the
weapons were sent for forensic examination and as per
the report of forensic lab, human blood was found on the
knife, Pants, and the "Angocha".
23. Considering that there was a very strong
motive, eyewitness evidence in the form of PW 5 and the
recovery, we are of the opinion that the prosecution has
proved its case against accused Bablu beyond a
reasonable doubt and to that extent the appeal of the
appellant Bablu is liable to be dismissed. The conviction
and sentence awarded by the learned trial court, as far as
it relates to appellant Hari Singh @ Bablu, is hereby
affirmed. His appeal is hereby dismissed. He is in jail and
shall undergo the period of sentence awarded by the trial
court.
24. As regarding appellant Kamal Singh, under the
facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion
that the prosecution has not been able to prove its case
beyond a reasonable doubt against the appellant Kamal
Singh. The doubt belongs to the accused. He was liable to
be given a benefit of doubt in this case, as we accept the
submission of the learned counsel for the accused Kamal
that the testimony of PW 2 against him cannot be trusted,
and so is the case with the recovery. The star witness PW
5 also did not disclose his name on the same day to her
father, and her testimony only so far as it relates to Kamal

14
Singh appears to be an afterthought. His presence hence
becomes doubtful. Doubt belongs to the accused and we
believe the accused/appellant Kamal Singh was liable to
be given a benefit of doubt.
25. Consequently, the appeal of the appellant
Kamal Singh is liable to be allowed and is hereby allowed.
The judgment and order dated 16.09.2015 passed by the
Trial Court in Session Trial No. 141 of 2014 so far as it
relates to conviction and sentence to accused Kamal Singh
is set aside, and the accused/appellant Kamal Singh is
acquitted of the charge under Section 302 read with
Section 34 I.P.C. The accused/appellant Kamal Singh is in
jail. He shall be released forthwith unless wanted in any
other case.
26. Let a copy of this judgment along with the
Lower Court Record be sent to the court concerned for
onward compliance.
(Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.) (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
Avneet/ 29.03.2019
